from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Three Perspectives", [
            "Powers, roots, and logs are three perspectives.",
            "They describe the same relationship: base, exponent, result.",
            "Think of this as a triangle of operations."
        ])

        # Create nodes
        power_node = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.5, color="#FF6600", fill_opacity=0.6), Text("Power", font_size=20))
        root_node = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.5, color="#33CC33", fill_opacity=0.6), Text("Root", font_size=20))
        log_node = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.5, color="#3399FF", fill_opacity=0.6), Text("Log", font_size=20))

        # Position nodes (Triangle)
        self.place_at_grid(power_node, 'B3')
        self.place_at_grid(root_node, 'D2')
        self.place_at_grid(log_node, 'D4')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(FadeIn(power_node), FadeIn(root_node), FadeIn(log_node))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        # Create connecting lines
        line1 = Line(power_node.get_center(), root_node.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        line2 = Line(root_node.get_center(), log_node.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        line3 = Line(log_node.get_center(), power_node.get_center(), color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2), Create(line3))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Roots help us find the base.", "Think of roots as undoing exponents.", "If two cubed is eight, cube-root eight is two."]
        self.setup_layout("The First Twist: Roots as Inverse Powers", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Roots help us find the base.
        eq1 = MathTex("y^{1/n} = x", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq1, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Think of roots as undoing exponents.
        eq2 = MathTex("x^n = y", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(eq2, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Transform(eq1, eq2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # If two cubed is eight, cube-root eight is two.
        eq3 = MathTex("2^3 = 8", "\\rightarrow", "8^{1/3} = 2", color=GREEN)
        self.place_in_area(eq3, 'C2', 'D5', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq1, eq3))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Final Twist: Logarithms as Time-Keepers", [
            "Logs help us find the exponent.",
            "They act as our time-keeper.",
            "How many doubles to reach eight? Three."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        log_eqn = MathTex(r"\log_b(y) = x", font_size=48)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Logs help us find the exponent.
        self.play(FadeIn(log_eqn))
        self.place_at_grid(log_eqn, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#3399FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # They act as our time-keeper.
        log_eqn.set_color_by_tex("log", "#3399FF")
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#3399FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # How many doubles to reach eight? Three.
        example = MathTex(r"\log_2(8) = 3", font_size=48)
        self.place_at_grid(example, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(example))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#3399FF"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Connection: The Universal Equation", 
                          ["Three operations, one mathematical story.", 
                           "Shift your focus to find the unknown.", 
                           "Powers, roots, logs: linked forever."])
        
        # Define equations
        eq_pow = MathTex("2^3 = 8", color=YELLOW)
        eq_root = MathTex("\\sqrt[3]{8} = 2", color="#00FFFF")
        eq_log = MathTex("\\log_2(8) = 3", color=PINK)
        
        eqs = VGroup(eq_pow, eq_root, eq_log)
        
        # Position in a triangle
        self.place_at_grid(eq_pow, "B4", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(eq_root, "D3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(eq_log, "D5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        cycle_arrow = CurvedArrow(eq_pow.get_bottom(), eq_root.get_right(), radius=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(eq_pow), FadeIn(eq_root), FadeIn(eq_log))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(Indicate(eq_pow), Indicate(eq_root), Indicate(eq_log))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PINK))
        self.play(Create(cycle_arrow))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Mathematical Trinity: Powers, Roots, and Logarithms

sections.title: Introduction: The Three Perspectives of a Number
sections.content: Briefly introduce the relationship between x^y = z. Explain that if we treat the base, the exponent, or the result as the 'unknown', we get three different operations: Power (result), Root (base), and Logarithm (exponent). Use an animation of a triangle where each corner represents one of these operations.
sections.example: Imagine a tree growing: Power calculates its height over time, Root calculates how long it has been growing, and Logarithm calculates the growth rate needed to reach a specific height.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Exponential Foundation
sections.content: Define the base exponential form b^x = y. Visualize this as a 'Growth Machine' where 'b' is the input, 'x' is the intensity, and 'y' is the output.
sections.example: 2^3 = 8. (Base 2, Exponent 3, Result 8). Visual: A stack of 2x2x2 cubes forming a larger 8-unit cube.

sections.title: The First Twist: Roots as Inverse Powers
sections.content: Transition from b^x = y to finding the base: y^(1/x) = b. Explain how the root 'undoes' the power. Show a graphical animation of a square expanding into a cube and then collapsing back to its side length.
sections.example: If 2^3 = 8, then 8^(1/3) = 2. A robot vacuum cleaner clears a path of 8 square units; the root tells us the side length of the square path (2 units).

sections.title: The Final Twist: Logarithms as Time-Keepers
sections.content: Explain that log_b(y) = x asks 'How many times must I multiply the base to get the result?' This is the 'Time' variable of the exponential equation. Emphasize that logs are just exponents in disguise.
sections.example: log_2(8) = 3. Using a digital timer: If a bacteria colony doubles (base 2) to reach a population of 8, the log tells us exactly 3 cycles passed.

sections.title: Summary and Connection: The Universal Equation
sections.content: Synthesize the three forms into one visual 'Conversion Cycle' animation. Reinforce that these are not separate entities, but three ways to view the same mathematical relationship.
sections.example: A summary graphic showing a triangle: [2^3=8] -> [8^(1/3)=2] -> [log_2(8)=3]. Each arrow represents shifting the 'unknown' focus.
